chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife, and she became separate from him, and she had a daughter who was a slave-girl, and he bought her; is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Is a man permitted to marry his divorced wife's daughter if he buys her from slavery?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the specific legal mechanism of 'illah (effective cause) in the prohibition of marriage, demonstrating that the father's purchase of his divorced wife's slave daughter creates a distinct barrier to marriage, separate from the general prohibition of the daughter of the wife. It highlights the Shia juristic focus on how changes in ownership status (from slave to free via purchase) interact with kinship ties to establish permanent marital prohibitions. The ruling underscores the precision of Usuli jurisprudence in distinguishing between prohibitions arising from direct lineage versus those arising from marital alliances and property relations.
